oewn-08281818-n.learner: a group of people who are together for a while to do something
examples: I have reason to expect an addition to our family party.
A party of us set out early to search the woods.

oewn-08269523-n.learner: a group of people who have come together to enjoy themselves
examples: It was at Sir William Lucas's, where a large party were assembled.

oewn-07462241-n.learner: an event where people can come together to be with others and have fun
examples: They gave a party at Netherfield to celebrate the wedding.

oewn-15228587-n.learner: a length of time made up of 365 days, or 366 in some years
examples: How many letters you must have occasion to write in the course of a year!
For about three years I heard little of him.

oewn-15229093-n.learner: a fixed part of the calendar year that is set aside each year for one kind of activity
examples: The school year begins in September and ends in June.

oewn-15226340-n.learner: the time a planet takes to travel once all the way around the sun
examples: A year on Mars is nearly twice as long as a year on Earth.

oewn-00957180-v.learner: to have something in mind that you are trying to say or get across
examples: When I said she was quiet, I meant that she rarely spoke in company.

oewn-00710367-v.learner: to have something in your mind as the purpose of what you do
examples: She meant to write to her aunt that evening, but forgot.

oewn-00933814-v.learner: to have something as its direct sense, or to suggest it along with that
examples: In this letter, "shortly" means within the week.

oewn-01829179-v.learner: to feel a strong wish for something
examples: "And Lydia used to want to go to London," added Kitty.
I do so want papa to take us all there for the summer!

oewn-02638648-v.learner: to be without something, or to have less of it than is needed
examples: Sense and Sensibility has perhaps the fewest out-and-out admirers; but it does not want them.
This old coat wants mending before the winter.

oewn-08683242-n.learner: a built-up place with set edges that is smaller than a city
examples: They stopped for the night at a small town on the road north.

oewn-08243435-n.learner: all the people who live in a town
examples: The whole town turned out to watch the soldiers march past.

oewn-08689937-n.learner: one of the parts a county is divided into for local government
examples: The town votes each spring on how its money will be spent.

oewn-13987306-n.learner: the state of being a married couple, joined by choice for life or until they divorce
examples: Happiness in marriage is entirely a matter of chance.

oewn-01039028-n.learner: the act of getting married, or the ceremony in which it is done
examples: Their marriage took place in the village church on a Tuesday morning.

oewn-08005815-n.learner: the two people who are married to each other
examples: His second marriage was a good deal happier than his first.

oewn-01560454-a.learner: smallest in amount, in extent, or in degree; it is the form of "little" that means the smallest of all, and it usually comes after "the"
examples: I do not reckon the notice and kindness of Lady Catherine de Bourgh as among the least of the advantages in my power to offer.

oewn-07560035-n.learner: a good, warm feeling of liking someone or something
examples: I think it would not be very likely to promote sisterly affection or delicacy of mind.
He then shut the door, and, coming up to her, claimed the good wishes and affection of a sister.
it is felt to be the right and proper thing to love them
Helping her home was the kindest thing he did that day.

oewn-04431553-n.learner: something that is not given a name of its own
examples: A dark thing lay in the road ahead, and no one could say what it was.

oewn-04431353-n.learner: an object that people have made
examples: He opened the box and set the small brass thing on the table.

oewn-00073433-r.learner: only a little short of it, but not quite done or not quite so
examples: she would have felt almost sure of success if he had not been to leave Hertfordshire so very soon
She is almost three-and-twenty!
